component.name: Lolly
component.summary: Generate on-brand creative assets from simple inputs

description.p: Lolly is a constraint-first, template-driven tool for generating on-brand creative assets - QR codes, charts, diagrams, event badges, documents, filters and more - as PNG, SVG, PDF or video. Everything renders on your device; nothing is uploaded.

screenshot.caption: The tool gallery - every tool is data, not bundled code
Utilities for everyday jobs: verify, unpack, convert, capture
The brand studio - colours, type and tokens define what every tool renders
Export to PNG, SVG, PDF or video, rendered on your device

description.p: Lolly files now use one manifest-led opening flow across the app and operating system. Shared designs, design systems and brand workspaces are identified before import, with measured size and content details.

ul.li: Large bundles are inspected without expanding their payload first, then verified once after confirmation.
Design systems import separately without replacing existing systems; cancelled file pickers make no changes.
Finder and Linux file managers recognise Lolly documents, while supported third-party formats remain alternate opening choices.

description.p: A formal release across every platform. The design-system studio now starts with one colour and grows as you add to it; what shipped is tagged Starter and what you chose is tinted; the first colour is a picker; a Google Font previews on the first press; swatches can be selected in bulk by dragging across the palette.

ul.li: Design tool: one motion model, a top bar, a navigator and an inspector; text animation with native PowerPoint export; tilt, Choreograph showcases and camera moves; sub-slide stacks and transcript-driven editing.
Sequence audio: pan, crossfades, signal-following ducking, a true-peak limiter, pitch-preserving time-stretch, a three-band EQ, loudness normalisation and an effect rack with on-device voice cleanup.
Narrated slides: speaker notes become a voice track, captions travel in the file, PPTX carries real slide audio and a deck exports as a SCORM package.
lolly:// deep links open a tool with its inputs filled from another app, a shortcut or a QR code.
The service worker heals cache entries that left on-device models stuck at 100% for returning users.

description.p: Version alignment across every Lolly shell - desktop, mobile and the control plane now share one number - plus two fixes carried in from the web shell:

ul.li: In a narrow export panel the Copy, Save and Share actions collapse cleanly to their icons again, keeping their meaning through tooltips and screen-reader labels. They previously tried to stack as full-width labelled rows, which only half-applied and overflowed the sheet.
Vector export is more faithful: text stroke and paint-order are honoured, and transformed elements decompose correctly, so SVG and PDF output better matches what is on screen.

description.p: This build also carries the 1.0.3 fixes forward - the bundled tray indicator library and the guard that skips the tray rather than aborting startup, openSUSE Leap 16 packages, and a native aarch64 Debian package.
Fixes a crash on startup. No change to what the app renders or exports:

ul.li: The system tray loads its indicator library lazily, so nothing in the build could catch that the Flatpak did not ship it. The app started and died immediately. It is now bundled.
The RPM never declared that library as a dependency, so it could install on a system without it and hit the same crash. It does now.
If the library is ever missing anyway, the tray is skipped with a warning instead of aborting startup.

description.p: Packaging fix, no change to what the app renders or exports:

ul.li: The Flatpak build now carries the same desktop integration the RPM and Debian packages already shipped - the .lolly file association, the GNOME Files thumbnailer and the GNOME Shell search provider.

description.p: At home on the Linux desktop:

ul.li: .lolly files open from the file manager, with thumbnails for shared sessions
lolly:// links deep-link straight into tools
Pick colours from anywhere on screen - the eyedropper now reaches every window
Set any render as your wallpaper, with your desktop confirming first
Find tools from GNOME search and KRunner
A tray shortcut turns a copied link into a QR code - the clipboard is read only when you click
Watch a hot folder to pull new files into your uploads

description.p: First packaged release: the full tool gallery and brand studio, with on-device export to PNG, SVG, PDF and video.
